checkpoint.label: Labor Day gate
checkpoint.decision: Whether 1:20 stays alive into the final 8 weeks. ALL criteria must hold. Miss any → race committed at 1:24-1:27 with zero regret. Honest prior even with perfect execution: passes ~1 in 5.
checkpoint.math: 1:20 needs a ~36:18 10K-equivalent on race day. 37:30 eight weeks out ≈ 1:22:30 equivalent — ~3% left to find, the outer edge of realistic. 38:30 ≈ 1:24:50 ≈ needing ~5 min in 8 weeks: arithmetic-dead. His 10K historically OVERSTATES his half fitness (35:33 vs ~1:30-1:35 demonstrated) — endurance is the side to distrust.

profile.signature: Chronically intensity-heavy, easy-running deficient — trains like a 25 mi/wk runner doing 45 mi/wk of intensity. 2022 easy/recovery was ~12% of volume; last 12 months ≈54% at tempo+; Q2 2026 was 45% threshold, 13% interval/race, ~7.5% easy. Races fast off low mileage — then every build ends in a crash. No polarization anywhere in the log.
profile.the_deficit: Aerobic base. A 35:33-10K engine attached to ~1:30 endurance. Base volume at genuinely easy effort is the single highest-value thing he can do, and the thing he most resists.
profile.execution_pattern: Negotiates prescribed easy paces upward, then drifts 20-30 s/km faster as a run progresses. The failure mode is holding the ceiling LATE, not starting too fast.
profile.consistency_risk: Life-schedule crunch, not motivation or body. Plans must survive busy weeks — short easy runs beat perfect weeks. Protect the Tuesday club anchor.

cadence.why: A cheap Achilles-load lever — shorter stride at the same pace lowers peak tendon force.

achilles.status: Remodeled and demonstrably load-tolerant at 25+ months — track reps at 4:06/km, a 21.1 km TT, repeated threshold work, no incident. NOT to be treated as post-op fragile.
achilles.maintenance: Heavy-slow weighted calf work 2x/wk as performance insurance, not rehab.
achilles.ramp_caution_reason: General tissue adaptation (a body adapted to ~12 mi/wk being asked to carry 40) plus the documented boom-bust history — which predates the injury. NOT tendon fragility.

timeline.lesson: Two failure modes, repeatedly: (1) intensity stacked on a base too thin to absorb it, and (2) life-schedule squeezes that break the block. Neither is a tendon problem. The counter-strategy is unglamorous easy volume, a protected social anchor, and plans that survive a bad week.

protocols.strength: Heavy-slow weighted calf raises (straight-leg + bent-knee, slow eccentric, 3-4 × 8-10 hard) 2x/wk — the one item to nag about. Hips/core 2x/wk, covered by the daily 7-min bodyweight circuit. That circuit's 30 s bodyweight calf raises do NOT satisfy the calf protocol (endurance stimulus ≠ heavy-slow tendon stimulus). No plyometrics — track work already supplies elastic load.
protocols.weight: Daily fasted weigh-in; interpret the 7-day rolling average only. Target ~128-130 lb by October. Alarm: >0.3 kg/wk loss + rising RHR + sagging HRV = under-fuelling, intervene. Worth ~1-2 s/km per kg at HM effort.
protocols.quality_budget: Proportion, not day-count. Quality must sit on enough easy volume to absorb it. At ~15 mi/wk, club + long run is already most of the week. If the long run is run hard, one other quality slot is forfeited that week.
protocols.sat_tempo_gates: 4+ consecutive weeks at 35+ mi/wk, zero Achilles symptoms through a full block, HRV near ~87 and RHR stable while absorbing existing quality. Expected mid-to-late September — deliberately late, since weeks 12-15 are when HM-specific tempo pays most.
protocols.decoupling_marker: Aerobic decoupling on steady long runs is the secondary fitness marker. Jul 5 baseline ~6% at 5:24/km. Target <5% at 5:45, trending toward 5:15-5:30 at stable HR by September — that closing IS the base being built.

prediction_protocol: One number per day. Basis: current threshold estimate, 5K shape conversion, minus an endurance discount for the volume/long-run deficit, cross-checked against the Nov 2025 benchmark (1:33:42 @ CTL 25). Volume and long-run length move it fastest early (~30-60 s per clean 25+ km week); threshold work matters later; missed weeks move it backward fastest. Credit only what is repeatable — no credit for excess intensity on easy days. Never move it >30 s/day without a race/TT or a missed week.

pace_curve_1y._note: Best elapsed time (s) per distance (m), all runs, rolling 1-year window ending 2026-07-26, from athlete_pace_curves_get. Cross-validated vs RUNNER_CONTEXT §4: 1mi 5:54, 5K 19:17, 10K 42:41. Unchanged over the last two weeks — recent work has been aerobic, not max-effort.

critical_speed_model._note: CS/D' fit by Intervals.icu on the 1-year pace curve (r²=0.99997). CS 4.273 m/s = 3:54/km. Short-duration-biased for a low-volume athlete — read as a ceiling marker, not a threshold prescription.
